rsa_ladder.label: 15 = 3 x 5
rsa_ladder.method: Shor's algorithm on 7-qubit NMR quantum computer

rsa_ladder.label: 21 = 3 x 7
rsa_ladder.method: Shor's algorithm on photonic quantum computer
rsa_ladder.note: Largest number factored by Shor's on quantum hardware

rsa_ladder.label: ~100-bit semiprime
rsa_ladder.signal: Proves the physics works at meaningful scale without classical shortcuts

rsa_ladder.label: RSA-512
rsa_ladder.signal: THE CANARY. Hockey stick begins. Breaking RSA becomes an engineering problem.

rsa_ladder.label: RSA-1024
rsa_ladder.signal: Legacy systems fall. Mass migration urgency.

ecdlp_ladder.label: 6-bit ECDLP
ecdlp_ladder.method: Shor's variant on public quantum cloud hardware
ecdlp_ladder.note: Prior largest public quantum ECDLP attack before April 2026

ecdlp_ladder.label: 15-bit ECDLP (Bitcoin-style key)
ecdlp_ladder.method: Shor's variant on ~70-qubit public cloud quantum device
ecdlp_ladder.source: Giancarlo Lelli, Project Eleven Q-Day Prize (1 BTC bounty, April 2026)
ecdlp_ladder.note: First non-trivial quantum ECDLP attack; ~512x prior 6-bit public record. Key space 32,767; recovered in minutes.

ecdlp_ladder.label: 64-bit ECDLP
ecdlp_ladder.signal: Proof of concept for quantum ECDLP

ecdlp_ladder.label: 128-bit ECDLP
ecdlp_ladder.signal: THE CANARY. Engineering sprint begins. Blockchain migration race starts.

ecdlp_ladder.label: 256-bit ECDLP (secp256k1)
ecdlp_ladder.signal: Q-DAY (Blockchain). Bitcoin and Ethereum keys breakable.

classical_context.label: RSA-250 (829 bits)
classical_context.note: Largest RSA number factored by any method

resource_estimates.note: Resource estimates do NOT advance the canary ladders (no hardware demonstration). They track how much hardware would be required to perform a break given current algorithmic best-known. Trend matters: estimates have fallen ~5 orders of magnitude in 20 years.

ecdlp_secp256k1.source: Google Quantum AI + Ethereum Foundation + Stanford — 'Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies against Quantum Vulnerabilities' (ZK-disclosed)
ecdlp_secp256k1.note: 10x spacetime improvement over prior art. Optimization initially hidden behind a Groth16 SNARK / SP1 zkVM proof — first use of ZK for academic censorship.

ecdlp_secp256k1.source: Cain et al. (Oratomic / Caltech / UC Berkeley) — 'Shor's algorithm is possible with as few as 10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits' (arXiv:2603.28627)
ecdlp_secp256k1.note: Coordinated release with Google paper. Applies Google's logical optimizations + neutral-atom physical optimizations. Five orders of magnitude below 2017 estimate.

ecdlp_secp256k1.source: Schrottenloher — 'Optimized Point Addition Circuits for Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithms' (arXiv)
ecdlp_secp256k1.note: Independent rediscovery of Google's secret optimization 2 months after publication; confirms the claim is real. Craig Gidney concurrently disclosed he held the same optimization under censorship pressure for a year.
Crowdsourced optimization using Google's ZK verifier as automated reward function. AI-driven 'autoresearch' contributions from non-experts (incl. a teenager). Compounding micro-optimizations ongoing.

public_qday_estimates.source: NSA / NIST — federal PQC migration deadline 2035
public_qday_estimates.note: Standard US gov reference date for forced migration off vulnerable crypto

public_qday_estimates.source: Justin Drake (Ethereum Foundation, Google paper co-author) — 50% odds of Q-Day by 2032, 10% by 2030
public_qday_estimates.note: Drake calls the NIST 2035 date 'a joke' that 'should be discounted entirely'. References non-public information.
